$comment: Riftlight authored opening draft. Development preview only; see ../README.md. Production campaign id will be riftlight. No bonus XP: preserve the design bible campaign budget.
title: Snow on the Quay

goal.text: Find out where the snow on the quay is coming from.

steps.label: Find where the cold comes from

market.narration: The Exchange has put its stalls back along the quay. A noodle seller lifts her awning with a broom. Then a snowflake lands in your breakfast. The sky is clear! Snow should not be falling at all. Today's job: find out where this snow is coming from. "First, I need hands!" calls the noodle seller. "This awning is heavy, and I pay in coins."

awning_plan.narration: Snow piles up on the awning. It sags like a hammock, and the poles wobble. "Quick!" says the noodle seller. "Before it all lands in my broth!" How will you save it?

awning_lift.prompt: Everyone take a pole! Lift together on the noodle seller's count: one, two, UP!

awning_tie.prompt: Tie each corner rope to the stall rail before the next gust. Fast fingers win.

awning_brace.prompt: Brace holds the middle pole still. Can you haul the saggy cloth tight around it?

awning_up.narration: The awning snaps tight, and the snow whooshes off onto a crate. The noodle seller drops three coins in your hands, then wraps up a supper bundle: flatbread, cheese and a sausage. "For later. Don't tell the pot. The pot thinks everything is for the pot."

awning_flap.narration: The awning flaps like a huge wet bird. A pot of broth tips into the gutter. The noodle seller ties the cloth down herself. "That is for trying," she says, and gives you one coin. The pot gurgles in a hurt way.

noodle_counter.narration: Her stall smells of ginger and honey. "Honeycake is three coins," says the noodle seller. "Questions are free. Go look at the fish stall, the gull on the post and that ship. They are all wrong this morning."

noodle_buy.narration: She slides a honeycake into a paper twist and counts your coins twice, just for fun. "Eat it warm, or save it for somebody who needs it." A snowflake lands on the cake and melts at once.

morning.narration: Snow falls over one fish stall, under a clear sky. On a mooring post, a gull shakes frost off its wings. "Cold," it grumbles. Beyond it, a ship has docked a day early. Its kitsune captain is arguing with the harbor clock. Where do you look first?

fish.narration: The fish seller holds up a scoop of snow. "I ordered ice. Ice stays where you put it." Under her table, stiff white grass has pushed up between the boards, cold enough to sting. "Somebody move my buckets, before my fish catch cold!"

fish_buckets.prompt: Pass the buckets down the line and under the awning, before the fish catch cold!

fish_help.narration: Every bucket reaches the noodle awning. The fish seller gives you two coins. "Something stepped off that patch of grass," she says. "Little hooves. Went that way." Wet hoofprints trail off between the crates.

fish_slosh.narration: A bucket tips, and fish flop across the boards. Everyone chases them with nets, hats and one noodle ladle. "Nobody lost a fish," says the fish seller, "but I lost count." She gives you a coin. "Something stepped off that grass. Little hooves. Went that way." Wet hoofprints lead off between the crates.

gull.narration: The gull stands on one foot. "Cold," it says. It changes feet. "Still cold." Its stomach growls. "That is the wind," it says. "Not my stomach." Below it, a small white hoofprint marks the boards.

gull_help.narration: The gull tucks its icy feet into your sleeve. "For the record, I did not ask to be a winter bird." From your arm, it spots more hoofprints between the crates.

gull_fed.narration: The gull gulps the crumbs and fluffs up to twice its size. "Best thing all day." It flaps onto a crate and points its beak. "Hoofprints! Little ones! That way!" Then, quieter: "Don't tell the other gulls I said thank you."

ship.narration: The captain spreads a chart over a barrel. "Our island was here yesterday. This morning the dock was over there. Same island. Same laundry. Wrong patch of sky." The wind tugs the chart. "Captain Thimble. If you find out why, tell me first."

chart_pin.prompt: The wind grabs the chart! Pin down the corners before it sails into the harbor.

ship_help.narration: You hold the corners while Captain Thimble ties the chart down. She hands you a spare ship's whistle. "A brave whistle. Loud enough to wake a whale. Blow it if you need help fast. And look for me if you reach the islands. You'll know my washing." A gust brings the smell of snow.

ship_flap.narration: The chart flaps away like a big pale bird. Captain Thimble dives and sits on it. "Never trust a map on a windy day," she puffs. "Look for me if you reach the islands. You'll know my washing." A gust brings the smell of snow.

ship_cold.narration: The captain points past the noodle stall. "The wind comes from between those crates. Wind should have more room than that." A coil of rope starts sliding across the boards toward them. She stamps on it. The rope stops, and sulks.

trail_check.prompt: Snow, frost and small hoofprints all lead along the quay, and fresh flakes are covering them. Which marks are newest?

trail_found.narration: The newest prints are crisp, no bigger than a plum, with white fuzz stuck in one. They skid sideways, as if something had tugged their owner. Then a deep horn blows from the water.

trail_lost.narration: Snow covers the marks before you can read them, and you end up with a boot full of slush. A barrel rolls a little way by itself, then stops. Then a deep horn blows from the water.

delivery.narration: The barge bumps the quay. The pilot points at stone landing steps hanging crooked above the water. "That was my landing this morning! Now it's halfway up a wall." Sacks of potatoes slide across his deck. "Supper for six boats. Help me!"

sack_line.prompt: Make a line and pass the sacks hand to hand. Keep the same pace, or the potatoes pile up! The pilot counts: nine, ten, ten, eleven.

sack_rally.prompt: A songkeeper's rally sets the beat. Can you pass every sack on the beat?

moor_ring.prompt: Find a mooring ring low enough to reach and strong enough to hold. Then loop the line the right way.

moor_wings.prompt: Wings carry the rope to a high ring. Can you pull the knot tight before the barge drifts?

delivery_sacks.narration: The potato sacks reach the quay. "Six crews eating tonight," says the pilot. He hands you a glass jar of glowing moss. "Mosslight. It glows when it's happy." The jar hums like a polite kettle. He frowns at the crooked steps. "Still need a way home."

sacks_dropped.narration: A sack bursts. Potatoes bounce off boots and plop into the harbor. At last the supper is ashore, though three potatoes went swimming. "Six crews eating tonight," says the pilot. "Mostly." He frowns at the crooked steps. "Still need a way home."

delivery_moor.narration: You tie the barge to a low mooring ring. The pilot tosses you a carved charm that smells like rain. "For the river. It keeps your feet sure on wet boards." Then he frowns at the crooked steps. "Now, where did my landing go?"

moor_drift.narration: The line slips, and the barge thumps the quay. Every sack hops. You tie it to the next mooring ring, with everyone's thumbs on the knot. A small crab in the hull complains. The pilot frowns at the crooked steps. "Now, where did my landing go?"

landing_steps.narration: The crooked steps tip off the wall like a stair that fell asleep standing up. A thin, cold breath slips out from under them. It smells of snow. "Whatever grabbed my landing didn't take it far," says the pilot. "Could somebody look?"

landing_climb.prompt: Grab the wet stone edge and haul yourself up. Can you hang on long enough to look underneath?

landing_prop.prompt: Which crates are the right size? Stack them so the steps rest on something solid.

landing_smash.prompt: Smash can knock a stuck step back into place. Can you hit the right spot without cracking it?

landing_clue.narration: Frost covers the underside of the steps like white feathers. Every feather points the same way: toward the far end of the quay. The pilot whistles. "Well, I'll be a pond. Thank you." He flips you two coins.

landing_slip.narration: Your foot skids, and the pilot catches your sleeve. Under the steps is only a puddle and a very surprised snail. "Never mind," he says. "Since this morning, the steps all lean toward the far end of the quay. I wish I knew why."

quay_rest.narration: The pilot tosses up a bag of warm potato skins, salty and perfect. You eat them on a crate. Behind the stalls, a ladder climbs the harbor master's house to the rooftops. From up there comes a lot of cawing, all of it on purpose.

rookery.narration: You climb out onto the rooftops. Crows sit on every chimney pot, staring at you. A sign says NO MESSING. (WITH US.) This rooftop school is called the Rookery. Here crows train each Duskrunner, a hero who runs quick and quiet. "Wipe your feet," they say, pointing at a tiny doormat. On a peg hangs a dusk hood, soft as a shadow. Worn with a star circlet, it only itches. "Try it on, if you like. But nobody who leaves the Exchange finds our ladder again."

variants.text: The crows of the Rookery eye you from every chimney. "Back again." The sign still says NO MESSING. (WITH US.) The dusk hood waits on its peg. You wipe your feet on the tiny doormat. "Remember: once you leave the Exchange, our ladder is gone."

rookery_lesson.narration: The crows show you how to cross the roof without a sound. Step on the moss. Never the loose tile. Nothing clatters. Back at the ladder, you find a folded note in your pocket: "Saw that. Nice. Don't mess with us."

quay.narration: At the end of the quay, two stacks of crates lean toward a thin fold in the air. A loose rope slides across the wet boards toward it. From the fold comes a deep, slow creak, and a hum like a note nobody is singing.

check_pattern.prompt: Can you spot which loose things will slide first?

onSuccess.narration: The rope, the barrel lid, the crates: everything leans toward the fold.

onFailure.narration: A barrel lid shoots past your ankle before you can point.

quay_slip.prompt: Vanish hides you in the shadows between the stacks. Can you see what leans toward the fold before it slides?

quay_lit.narration: The moss glows bright and curious. In its light, every shadow points the same way: toward the fold. You nudge a wedge under the nearest crate. One of the dock workers carries the jar off to light the rest of the quay. Beyond the crates, something small bleats.

pattern_seen.narration: You kick a wedge under the nearest crate and shout a warning. The noodle seller grabs her awning before it tears free. Beyond the crates, something small bleats.

pattern_missed.narration: The lid rolls in a circle, twice, and drops flat by the fold, very pleased with itself. You pull everyone back from its path. Beyond the crates, something small bleats.

clear_check.narration: You and the dock workers lead the market crowd behind the stall rail. The noodle seller points the way with her ladle. A cat on a barrel will not budge, so you carry the barrel.

clear_quay.narration: You lift the noodle awning clear of a sliding crate. The dock workers pass buckets out of the way. Beyond the crates, something small bleats.

crate_plan.narration: The nearest stack groans and leans toward the fold. Two dock workers hang off its rope, boots skidding. "We can't hold it!" Behind the stack, the small bleat comes again. If the crates slide, they land on whatever is bleating. Overhead, the gull shrieks that it saw this coming.

crate_haul.prompt: Grab the rope behind the dock workers! Dig in your heels and haul on three!

crate_wedge.prompt: Which plank, and where? Wedge it under the stack before the next groan.

whistle_call.narration: You blow the brave whistle. It is very, very loud. Pigeons leave the quay. Shutters slam. A dozen dock workers come running, grab the rope and lean. The stack creaks and stops. The whistle gives one last squeak and goes quiet for good.

crates_back.narration: The stack stops. The dock workers let go one finger at a time. One pats the top crate. "Good crate," she whispers. The fold still breathes cold, but nothing else slides. Behind the stack, the small bleat comes again, closer now, and a little cross.

crates_slid.narration: One crate slides into the fold and is gone with a soft pop. A cold puff comes back out. "Right," says one of the dock workers. "Nobody tell the crate's owner." The rest of the stack stops leaning. Behind it, the bleat comes again, closer and a little cross.

gap.narration: Between the two stacks is a narrow gap. At the far end, the air looks thin and wrinkled, like a curtain in a draft. The bleat comes from just beyond. You can squeeze through sideways, or climb over the lower stack.

gap_squeeze.prompt: Breathe in and slide through sideways without knocking a single crate.

gap_climb.prompt: Find handholds on the lower stack and haul yourself over. Don't wobble it!

gap_through.narration: You come out the other side without knocking a crate. The boards here are wet with frost, not water. A tuft of white fuzz sits on a nail. The bleat comes again, right in front of you.

gap_scrape.narration: You scrape through with a squeak. You lose a button and gain a splinter. The boards here are wet with frost, not water. A tuft of white fuzz sits on a nail. The bleat comes again, right in front of you.

shimmer.narration: The fold opens. Cold air pours out, smelling of very old ice. On the other side, snow lies under a white sky. So that is where the snow on the quay comes from! Beside your boots stands a snowhorn goat kid, hardly taller than a bucket. It tries to climb your leg. A faint light traces the edge of the fold.

kid_food.narration: You hold out a crust. The kid forgets everything else in the world and trots to your boots. It gobbles the crust in three bites and leans on your shin, warm and sticky. Behind you, a mooring rope draws tight.

read_light.narration: With a Starweaver's eyes, you study the light around the fold. It has a name: Riftlight. The kid stamps twice, waiting to be picked up. Behind you, a mooring rope draws tight.

pull.narration: The rope snaps straight. Crates scrape across the boards. The kid skids toward the opening, hooves spread wide. A dock worker throws you a loose line. "Grab this!" You have time for one move.

variants.text: The crate you wedged still holds, so you have a clear spot to plant your feet.
"You saved my fish. Let us save that little one!" calls the seller. She passes the loose line over the crates, where you can reach it without stepping into their path.
The barge pilot grabs a sliding potato sack before it hits your legs.
"Crate on your left!" calls the pilot from his moored boat. You step clear in time.

catch.prompt: Catch the kid before it reaches the fold.

onSuccess.narration: You scoop the kid up. Its hooves drum on your coat.

onFailure.narration: You catch a hoof, then the rest of the goat. A crate clips your shoulder.

anchor.prompt: Hold the line while everyone grabs on.

onSuccess.narration: You wrap the line around a mooring post. Everyone has a hand on it before the post gives.

onFailure.narration: The wet line slips. You grab the last loop, knock your knee, and pull the others with you.

swoop.prompt: Skyward or Glide lifts the kid. Can you keep the loose line clear of the sliding crates?

onSuccess.narration: Wings carry the kid clear of the crates. You guide the loose line past a cart wheel, keeping everyone together.

onFailure.narration: The line catches your foot and you bump your shoulder against a crate. Wings carry the kid clear anyway.

smash.prompt: Smash breaks a crate into a barrier. Can you guide the loose line around it?

onSuccess.narration: Wood cracks. You thread the line around the broken crate, and everyone gets time to hold on.

onFailure.narration: The broken crate skids away. The line pulls tight against your knee as you grab it.

brace.prompt: Brace holds the post steady. Can you keep the line taut while everyone gets a grip?

onSuccess.narration: The braced post holds. You take up the slack until everyone has the line. Then the boards lift.

onFailure.narration: The braced post holds, but the wet line slips through your hands and knocks you to your knees.

caught.narration: You tuck the kid against your chest. The dock worker lets go of her end of the line before it takes her too. You keep yours. The quay folds out of sight.

together.narration: The kid scrambles into the loop of rope between you. You pull it close. The line holds you together as the quay folds out of sight.

tumbled.narration: The kid lands against your chest. You tumble through together, dragging the loose end of the rope.

through.narration: For one breath there is no sound. Then your boots hit snow. You pull the kid inside your coat as the wind throws wet snow against your knees. It sneezes into your collar. Behind you, the fold pinches shut, and the harbor is gone. A small warm pulse waits in your hands.

ridge_walk.narration: The wind pushes like a giant hand. You knot your coat into a sling for the kid, and everyone takes a corner. A low ridge is a few steps away. Keep the sling level!

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your corner until the sling is level.
interaction.objectLabel: the kid in the coat sling

ridge_ok.narration: Linked together, you lean into the wind and walk. The ridge grows bigger. Behind it, the snow is quiet. The kid peeks out of the sling, sneezes, and looks very proud of itself.

ridge_drift.narration: The wind shoves, and you all slide across the snow in a heap, like a sled with elbows. You stop against the low ridge, laughing a little. The kid peeks out and looks proud of you anyway.

ridge_lee.narration: Behind the ridge, the wind drops to a mutter. The sky is the color of milk. The kid is shaking so hard its ears rattle. Warm it up first.

options.label: Tuck it in your coat
options.reaction: The kid burrows into the warm wool and sighs.

options.label: Rub its cold hooves
options.reaction: The kid kicks its warming hooves and bleats happily.

options.label: Hum a quiet tune
options.reaction: The kid's ears twitch in time to the tune.

onSuccess.narration: The shaking stops. One small ear pokes out of your collar and listens to the wind.

onFailure.narration: The kid wiggles free, sneezes, and burrows back in on its own.

white.narration: White slopes rise all around. Far below, water runs under a skin of ice. The kid peeks out at the empty snow and climbs straight back into your coat. Somewhere beyond the ridge, a bell rings.

barge_toss.narration: The horn belongs to a supply barge, sliding toward the quay too fast. Its frogfolk pilot waves a boat hook. "Throw me that rope! Right over my hook, if you please!"

interaction.cue: Tap when the rope is over the pilot's hook.

onSuccess.narration: The rope drops neatly over his hook. "Lovely," says the pilot, and hauls the barge in.

onFailure.narration: The rope plops into the harbor. The pilot fishes it out with his hook and hauls the barge in anyway.

sack_chain.narration: Six crews wait at their boats along the quay, and every one is hungry. "Pass the sacks friend to friend," says the pilot. "And mind the puddles. Potatoes hate puddles."

interaction.cue: Catch the sack, then pass it to the next friend.

onSuccess.narration: The sack sails from hand to hand without touching a puddle. Six crews cheer.

onFailure.narration: A sack lands in a puddle. A crew fishes it out and cheers anyway.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Captain Thimble: Chapter-scoped kitsune Sky Island captain, practical and brisk. Frustrated with a displaced island, kind to helpers. No explanation for the displacement.
npcVoices.The gull: Indignant, literal, chilly. Brief complaints; never explains the magic.
npcVoices.Fish seller: Practical, protective of fish and helpers. Short dockside speech.
